ai_summary.headline: Niger's 2026 HNRP is 20% funded, with multi-purpose cash barely present: $1.3m requested, $14k received.
ai_summary.narrative: Niger's 2026 HNRP asks for $675.6m on FTS and has received $135.3m, about 20% [s1][s2]. Multi-purpose cash is budgeted at $1.26m, 0.2% of requirements, and has received $14,247 [s1][s2]. Cash still moves at scale: the 2025 cash 4W records 1.3m people reached and 17.3bn FCFA, about $31m [s5], so most cash likely runs through sectoral lines that FTS does not separate. Sida reports restrictions on cash assistance are likely to continue in 2026 and that no MSNA was run in 2025 [s4]. Humanitarians must use escorts, and access is constrained [s6]. There is a CWG, which was revising the MEB in 2024 [s6], but I found no current leads, market monitoring or modality preference data. The only feasibility study is from 2020 and covers two regions [s7]. Requirements are also contested: the plan text cites $449m [s3] against $675.6m on FTS, which appears to include refugee response.
barriers: No 2025 MSNA, so no current preference evidence
Escort requirements and insecurity limit access
opportunities: Existing CWG and 4W reporting give a base to build on
Sida notes partners expect to use MPC where feasible
data_gaps: Plan status of OCHA presence not confirmed

total_funding_usd.note: All incoming funding to the plan, pledges excluded. Matches the FTS plan summary.

mpc_usd.note: FTS single-cluster view of the Transfert d’espèces à usages multiples cluster; shared-cluster view US$0.0M. Incoming flows, pledges excluded.

ctp_usd.note: All flows tagged 'Cash transfer programming (CTP)', inside or outside the MPC cluster.

sectoral_cva_usd.note: Flows whose FTS modality field is 'Cash transfer programming (CTP)' and whose destination cluster is not multi-purpose cash: 23 flows. The CTP tag is set by the reporting donor or agency and is not applied consistently, so this is a floor, not a measure of sectoral cash. Largest: Protection US$4.1M, Sécurité Alimentaire US$2.4M, Abris/NFI US$0.9M.

cva_usd.note: Union of the MPC cluster and the CTP tag. Widest defensible FTS cash figure; still a floor because untagged sectoral cash is invisible.

sectoral_cva_pct_of_total.note: sectoral_cva_usd as a share of total plan funding.

mpc_pct_of_total.note: MPC cluster funding as a share of total plan funding (single-cluster view).

fts_cva.caveat: FTS records funding, not transfers to people, and only to first-level recipients. Sectoral cash depends on a modality tag that reporters apply unevenly.

cva_to_local_pct.note: Indicator 4.2 proxy. Share of FTS cash funding (MPC cluster or CTP tag, US$7.6M) whose first-level recipient is a local or national NGO/CSO or a national government body. FTS does not see sub-grants, so this understates money that reaches local actors through international intermediaries.

all_funding_to_local_pct.note: Share of all plan funding whose first-level recipient is a local or national actor (US$5.9M). Same first-level caveat.

localisation.caveat: FTS sees first-level recipients only; indicator 4.2 as defined (direct donor allocation to local partners) is therefore a floor. Chair roles come from public CWG pages and may be out of date.
